definitions.back_to_back_period: device time per kernel of a long chain with CUDA events around the whole chain and no events between kernels; the kernel's service time plus that mode's per-kernel device-side gap
definitions.host_submission_cost: host wall time of the launch loop alone, taken with a monotonic clock immediately around the loop, before any synchronization and containing none
definitions.differenced_service_time: S_mode(k) = P_mode(k) - P_mode(nop), which removes that mode's per-kernel gap and leaves the kernel's marginal cost
definitions.clock_stationary_block: NVML SM clock equal immediately before and after the block, memory clock exactly 1593 MHz on both sides, throttle word zero on both sides

scored_expectations.claim: For each of g1, g2 and g4 at K = 256, S_graph(k) divided by S_eager(k) lies in [0.95, 1.05].
For g4 the raw ratio P_graph(g4) divided by P_eager(g4) lies in [0.97, 1.03].
P_eager(nop) divided by P_graph(nop) is at least 1.5.
An ordinary least squares fit of eager host loop time against K over K in [8, 256] returns R-squared of at least 0.99.
The fitted eager per-launch host slope lies in [0.8, 4.0] microseconds.
Graph replay host submission cost per replay at K = 256 divided by its value at K = 1 lies in [0.5, 2.0].
The fitted graph per-node host slope is at most 0.10 times the eager per-launch slope.
At K = 256 the graph host submission cost per enqueued kernel is at least 20 times smaller than the eager per-launch host cost.
The measured eager per-launch host cost differs from the Turing eager-host-bound point of 2,364,255 ps by more than 10 percent and is the smaller of the two.
P_graph(nop) at K = 256 divided by its value at K = 16 lies in [0.8, 1.25].
P_graph(nop) is at most 0.6 times the fitted eager per-launch host slope.
The graph makespan of one mix cycle equals the sum of its four members' graph makespans at the same K within 5 percent.
The eager makespan of one mix cycle equals the sum of its four members' eager makespans at the same K within 8 percent.

fatal_guards.claim: The job sees exactly one NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB, MIG disabled, ECC enabled, with no foreign compute process at the start or the end, and both the harness and nvidia-smi report the same GPU UUID.
Every reported number comes from clock-stationary blocks of a single clock state, with at least 8 such blocks, and no reported number averages across clock states.
Every CUDA graph instantiates successfully and reports exactly the node count its chain length implies, read back from the graph object rather than assumed.

Every device makespan is measured by CUDA events recorded inside the measured stream, and every host submission cost is measured by a host clock pair that contains no synchronization call and no event record.
No measured period is negative, and no GEMM period falls below its own two-sided roofline floor at the stage-1 HBM roof and the block's own clock-derived FLOP peak.
Every GEMM in the set returns the arithmetically correct result on a fixed element sample, checked once per kernel outside every timed region.
The batch-mean coefficient of variation of every reported period is at most 4 percent.
The eager and graph arms of a given kernel and chain length observe the same clock state.
